extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the DOE EFRC FY2026 NOFO (university PIs, research institutions, DOE national labs, non-profits, and industry partners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing Pre-Applications and full Applications in response to the DOE Energy Frontier Research Centers (EFRC) FY2026 Notice of Funding Opportunity (DE-FOA-0003614), including scope, eligibility, submission requirements, review criteria, and data-sharing expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific scope — discovery and use-inspired basic research
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications from multi-disciplinary teams are required to propose both discovery science and use-inspired basic research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section III of the NOFO for full scope. Applicants must propose both elements; ensure proposed work aligns with the NOFO objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic categories — BES Reports Topics and Special Topics
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two categories of topics: BES Reports Topics, and Special Topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For BES Reports Topics, see Sec. III of the NOFO for links to workshop and roundtable reports and which Priority Research Directions (PRD) or Priority Research Opportunities (PRO) should be addressed. Specific requirements for Special Topics are listed in Sec. III of the NOFO; eligibility is based on the special topic requirements (not all research areas in the BES reports are within scope for Special Topics).

rubrics_metrics.name: BES Reports Topics — address specified PRDs/PROs
rubrics_metrics.description: For the BES Reports topic, applicants must address the Priority Research Directions (PRD) or Priority Research Opportunities (PRO) identified in the referenced BES workshop and roundtable reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The webinar lists the applicable reports (e.g., Foundational Science to Accelerate Nuclear Energy; Controlling Subsurface Fractures and Fluid Flow; Basic Research Needs for Next Generation Electrical Energy Storage; Transformative Manufacturing; Microelectronics; Roundtables on Quantum Computing and Next-Generation Quantum Systems). Some reports specify which PRDs/PROs apply to New vs Renewal proposals — follow Sec. III for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Topics — defined topic list and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Special Topics for this NOFO are: Controlling Quantum Phenomena to Enable Unconventional Computing Paradigms; Development and Workflow Integration of AI/ML Models for Materials and Chemistry Discovery Science; Emergent Phenomena of Complex Chemical Systems; Fundamental Science for Critical Minerals and Materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility for proposals under a Special Topic is determined by the special topic requirements in the NOFO. Not all research areas referenced in BES reports are in scope for Special Topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicants and partner rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible Applicants: All types of domestic entities, including universities/colleges, non-profit organizations, for-profit organizations, DOE National Laboratories (see Sec. II of the NOFO). Other Federal agencies or FFRDCs may participate as partners (not lead institution). Non-domestic organizations may participate as partners (not lead), but must justify why the capability is not available domestically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead institution must be domestic. Awards are made to institutions, not to individual Directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition — multi-disciplinary and multi-institutional expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications are expected to involve multi-disciplinary research teams; multi-institutional applications are encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EFRC model couples basic research needs and grand-challenge science and often involves academic and national laboratory collaborations to accelerate scientific productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFRC Director eligibility and appointment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The director must be in a permanent or indefinitely extensible position at the applicant institution. University directors must be tenured at time of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each pre-application must designate a single EFRC Director. The EFRC Director named in the pre-application should not be changed in the full application unless unavoidable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Application requirement and submission limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A Pre-Application is required. Limits: 3 pre-applications per lead institution and 1 pre-application per Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-applications must be submitted via the DOE Portfolio Analysis and Management System (PAMS) by a user at the PI’s institution with the 'Submit to DOE' privilege. Late pre-application submissions are rarely accepted (see Sec. V.D.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Application page limit and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-applications are limited to five pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NOFO instructions for content and attachments. Pre-applications without required files (e.g., reviewer exclusion table) will be discouraged without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Application required attachments — reviewer-exclusion table and science topics spreadsheet
rubrics_metrics.description: NOFO requires a table of 'individuals who should not serve as reviewers' with the pre-application (guidance and template link are in Section IX.B.10 of the NOFO). Applicants should also attach the science topics spreadsheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the reviewer-exclusion table as a separate file, preferably in Excel format. Pre-applications without this table will be discouraged without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Application scientific content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-application science content should contain a clear and concise statement of the mission, scientific goals, and at least one scientific hypothesis or question motivating the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise and focused on research aims; emphasize novelty and how the center will address priority research directions/opportunities where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Application review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Any review of pre-applications will be based on the following criteria: Scientific and technical merit; Responsiveness to the objectives of the NOFO as stated in Section III; Appropriateness of the proposed research approaches; Likelihood of scientific impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews within a topical field will be comparative with priority given to scientifically innovative and forward-looking basic research with the highest likelihood of success as an application. Reviews will be conducted by no fewer than three subject matter experts under the direction of Federal program managers chosen for topical knowledge and breadth of perspective. Applicants with the highest rated pre-applications will be encouraged to submit full applications; applications not encouraged will be declined without merit review. Feedback about pre-applications will be provided upon request after selections are announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission requirements and portals
rubrics_metrics.description: Full Applications must be submitted via www.grants.gov by the specified deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that have not been encouraged by DOE (from the pre-application step) will be declined without merit review. Late submissions of applications are rarely accepted (see Sec. V.D.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application required tables (SF-424 field 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: NOFO requires two specific tables to be attached to field 12 of the SF-424 Research and Related Other Project Information form: (1) List of Individuals Who Should Not Serve as Reviewers (NOFO p.73) and (2) Summary budget (NOFO p.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications without these two tables may be declined without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget rule — lead institution funding request
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead institution must request more funding from DOE than any other team member for each 12-month budget period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that DOE makes awards to institutions, not to Directors. Structure budgets accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical sketches and current/pending support
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical sketch and list of current/pending support are required for each senior/key personnel; follow instructions in the NOFO, including the use of SciENcv (Science Experts Network Curriculum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a complete list of activities regardless of source of funding; follow NOFO formatting and content rules for biosketches and support statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing Plan (DMSP) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: New DMSP requirements for sharing digital scientific data went into effect for new solicitations on 10/1/2025. DMSP requirements include: validation and replication of results; timely and fair access; data repository selection; data management and sharing resources; and data sharing limitations. Publicly shared data must be reported to the Office of Scientific and Technical Information (OSTI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope emphasizes 'research data' to validate and replicate research findings; data underlying publications should be made as accessible as possible and available at time of publication; timeline for sharing other scientific data is required; repository selection should align with NSTC guidance. See DOE DMSP Guidance and SC DMSP Guidance for details and desirable characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award period, annual funding range, and Year 1 note
rubrics_metrics.description: Period of performance: Four years. Maximum/minimum award size: $3,000,000 to $4,500,000 per award per year. Average award size is expected to be $4,000,000 per award per year after the first year of operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For new applications, DOE will likely award less funding in Year 1 of the four-year project period than in subsequent years to account for ramp-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process mechanics for pre-applications
rubrics_metrics.description: SC may evaluate all or some portion of pre-applications to determine competitiveness within a scientific topic. Any such review will be conducted by no fewer than three subject matter experts under the direction of Federal program managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are comparative within topical fields; priority is given to scientifically innovative and forward-looking basic research with the highest likelihood of success as an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Late submissions of pre-applications and applications are rarely accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Sec. V.D.4 of the NOFO for the full late submission policy and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-domestic organization participation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-domestic organizations may participate as partners (not lead), but must justify why the capability is not available domestically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When including non-domestic partners, provide a compelling justification aligned with NOFO instructions; lead institution must remain domestic.
